analysis.subject: civics
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers the three federal branches, their membership and key roles, and how each branch checks the others through veto, confirmation, removal and judicial review.

overview.headline: Federal power is divided among three branches with checks and balances

keyPoints.point: The Constitution divides the federal government into legislative, judicial and executive branches.
keyPoints.quote: The Constitution of the United States divides the federal government into three branches:

keyPoints.point: The legislative branch is made up of Congress including the Senate and House of Representatives.
keyPoints.quote: The legislative branch is made up of Congress:

keyPoints.point: The judicial branch includes the Supreme Court and other federal courts that interpret laws and decide constitutional issues.
keyPoints.quote: The judicial branch includes the Supreme Court and other federal courts.

keyPoints.point: The executive branch is led by the president as head of state, leader of the executive branch and commander in chief of armed forces.
keyPoints.quote: The president is the head of state, leader of the executive branch, and commander in chief of the United States armed forces.

keyPoints.point: The system of checks and balances lets each branch respond to actions of the other branches.
keyPoints.quote: The ability of each branch to respond to the actions of the other branches is the system of checks and balances.
